items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: when I got in the band, I went to rehearsal at first there, they had, uh, Peter Arn was just the leader.

ctx.x: You never did join the WPA band then?

No, I was going to say, I always thought that was a little too slow money for me. I, I, well I should have because there wasn't nothing to it, you know. Most of the guys got in just for the money of it, you see. But like I say, then I was doing a little range, I was selling arrangements around you and everything, you know. But I, I, in other words, I was doing it just as good as those guys there, you see. So, and then another thing I, I didn't like it because the time that, like, you would get a good job, it…

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1979-12-05
items.q: They had Peter Bocard. And there was a lot of dissension in the band. Peter Bocard was the leader

ctx.x: These were the excursion boats, not the Password? The excursion boats, yeah. Not the Password.

Yeah, excursion boats. Somewhere when I got here in 48, they dropped us off in St. Louis and I was supposed to come back. But Piedhorn went with the band out there and the captain got discouraged. I forgot to repeat that. They had Peter Bocard. And there was a lot of dissension in the band. Peter Bocard was the leader and the Tramble Brothers was supposed to be the manager and they both came over the river and there was a lot of dissension. I could see and feel it. So when I went to Chicago, like I said, the…
What was it like playing on the boats? I mean, from what I heard, you know, I heard like one thing there were a lot of fights on the boats.

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: So Peter Bogart was lead, I think Eddie Pearson was sort of a manager, like, see. So I really missed Peter on that particular year, and we, that particular year we closed, we usually come back here, but we closed in St. Louis

ctx.x: Oh, that was in, let's see, about around 33. 33, yeah. So I remember Captain Boyne came over and talked to Peter on and told him he wanted to come down to the office and see him. You know, he said he'd like to have his band and he'd like to have him on the boat. And he spoke to me and he said, yeah, I said, that's sales. He said, sales have worked for us, which I had already worked with Pete Marvillin and sitting in there's being banned on the boat. So Peter on asked me about it. I told him, I said, well, that's…
